inlines.v: DISSECT, verb transitive [Latin , to cut.] 1. To cut in pieces; to divide an animal body, with a cutting instrument, by separating the joints; as, to dissect a fowl. Hence appropriately, 2. To cut in pieces, as an animal or vegetable, for the purpose of examining the structure and use of its several parts; to anatomize. Also, to open any part of a body to observe its morbid appearances, or to ascertain the cause of death or the seat of a disease. 3. To divide into its constituent parts, for the purpose of examination; as, dissect your mind; dissect a paragraph.
